fair_value.method: Blend of three methods for a Sept-2027 value: forward P/E $314 (50%: FY2028 EPS ~$10.30 x 30.5x), FCF yield $334 (30%: FY2028 FCF ~$135B at a 2.85% yield on ~14.2B shares) and a two-stage DCF $265 (20%: $128B FCF growing 8% for 10 years, 3.5% terminal, 8.5% WACC on a 5.1% risk-free rate). The blend is ~$312, down from $330 because of the rate regime and memory costs contracted through 2027.

methods.name: Forward P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028 EPS ~$10.30 (FY2026 ~$8.86, FY2027 consensus ~$9.58, then ~7.5% growth: mid-single-digit revenue, ~2.5% buyback shrink, gross margin held down by DRAM at ~$2.00/Gb through 2027) x 30.5x. This is a premium to Apple's ~28-30x 5-year average for services mix and AI/Duo optionality, but 5 turns below today's ~35.6x because the 10-year yield is above 5% and the Fed is hiking.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY2028 FCF ~$135B / 2.85% target FCF yield = ~$4.74T equity value / ~14.2B diluted shares in Sept 2027 = ~$334. Today's yield is ~2.4%, and I assume a modest decompression given 5%+ Treasuries.

methods.name: Two-stage DCF
methods.inputs: FCF $128B next year, growing 8%/yr for 10 years, 3.5% terminal growth, 8.5% WACC (5.1% risk-free plus ~3.4% risk premium). EV ~$3.5T, rolled forward one year on ~14.3B shares = ~$265. It shows that at current rates the price needs a lower discount rate or faster growth than fundamentals alone support. I give it low weight because Apple has persistently traded above textbook DCF.

bear.story: DRAM at ~$2.00/Gb (+33%) through 2027 squeezes gross margin to ~46%, and price increases on the iPhone 19 cycle hurt units. The Fed keeps hiking with the 10-year at 5%+, and the China chip-tariff step-up on 2027-06-23 comes in punitive. FY2027 EPS ~$9.1-9.3 and the multiple de-rates to ~25x FY2028 ~$9.8.

base.story: iPhone 18/Duo roughly meet expectations. Price increases mostly offset memory and gross margin holds ~47-48%. Services grows ~11-12% ex-FX (the slowdown is mostly FX) and the Google payment stays intact pending appeal. FY2028 EPS ~$10.4 on ~32.5x, a mild de-rating from 35.6x that roughly offsets EPS growth.

bull.story: Gemini-based Siri drives a multi-year upgrade cycle, Duo lifts ASPs, and pricing power more than covers memory so margins hold near 48% despite no cost relief. Yields fall back below 4.5% as inflation cools. FY2028 EPS ~$11.2 on ~37.5x.

thesis_break_reason: About 30% below $341 and under the 52-week low of $243.42. At $240 Apple is ~25x FY2027 consensus EPS of $9.58. With a 5%+ 10-year and a hiking Fed, a pure multiple compression to ~28x ($268) or even ~26.5x ($255) can happen without anything fundamental breaking, which is why I keep the break below the supervisor's $250. A close under ~$240 would most likely mean earnings estimates are being cut: gross margin guided below ~46% as $2/Gb DRAM outruns pricing, iPhone 18/19/Duo unit declines after price hikes, loss of the Google default-search payment, a forced App Store economics change, or a punitive China chip-tariff rate in June 2027.

key_uncertainties: Whether a ~35x forward multiple survives a Fed hiking cycle (3.75-4.00% after 2026-09-16) with the 10-year at ~5.0-5.2%
Memory: 2027 DRAM contracted at ~$2.00/Gb vs $1.50 (+33%), with no relief until at least mid-2028. Can price increases hold gross margin at 47-48% without hurting units?
Real demand for iPhone Duo and whether Gemini-based Siri drives an upgrade cycle

reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor's fact-checks, which I verified, moved me lower in three ways. (1) Rates: the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, the dot plot signals more hikes, and the 10-year closed above 5% (5.18% on the as-of date). I had no rate driver in round 1. A 35.6x P/E is a ~2.8% earnings yield against a 5%+ risk-free rate, so I cut my target multiple from 31.5x to 30.5x and added FCF-yield and DCF cross-checks. The DCF at an 8.5% WACC gives only ~$265, which shows how much the price relies on a low discount rate. (2) Memory: I confirmed that Apple accepted 2027 DRAM at ~$2.00/Gb (+30-40%) with no relief until mid-2028. My round-1 bull case assumed memory would roll over in 2027, which is wrong. I trimmed FY2028 EPS from $10.50 to ~$10.30 and cut the bull probability from 25% to 21%, and the bull case now relies on pricing power. (3) The June 2027 China chip-tariff step-up is a dated in-horizon event I had missed, so it adds a little mid-2027 left-tail weight. One finding moved me the other way. The supervisor says the services slowdown is mostly FX (a ~5pt drag, similar growth ex-FX), so I softened my round-1 structural services worry and base services is now ~11-12% ex-FX. The blended fair value is ~$312, down from $330. I do not expect the price to converge fully to fair value within 12 months because product-cycle momentum and record highs are real and the rate shock is already in the $341 close. So I set a median of ~$333 (about 60% of the way from fair value to today's price, plus 12 months of EPS growth). Scenario EV: 0.27x245 + 0.52x338 + 0.21x420 = ~$330. The ladder uses a lognormal with median $333 and sigma 0.28 (realized vol 25%, raised for the rate regime, the tariff date and the high starting multiple), with slightly fattened tails. P(>=341) = 0.47 (was 0.50), P(>=239) = 0.875 (was 0.89), P(>=409) = 0.225 (was 0.24). I keep the thesis break at $240 rather than $250: in a hiking cycle a de-rating into the mid-$250s is ordinary multiple risk, not a broken thesis. I did not consult option prices, implied volatility or anything under valuation/priors/.
